items.title: Joe Ascione interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: Mark Elf, guitarist, and I’m sure there were other — ... So I was there ... I see Mark Elf ... He said, “Man you can’t kick those tubs hard enough.” ... Next set so I boom- boom, start bashing.

ctx.x: So I always knew of him and Charlie Perry always used to say see if you can get to hook up with Billy. It never happened until a couple of years later, Sonny’s Jazz Club on Long Island had Billy do a Wednesday night steady gig for a while. And somehow I got the call from Sonny, the owner. And he said, “Hey, Joe” real raspy voice, scotch-ladened voice, you know “Joey, baby, come on here and play with Billy.” And I was nervous. So I’m sitting there and it’s I think Wes Belcamp and Pete Chivoli who used to play with…

I say, “Mark, what the hell’s this guy talking about? You’re the drummer, play the drums?” He said, “Man you can’t kick those tubs hard enough.” He said, “He’s played with Blakey and Elvin and Buddy Rich” and this and this. items.title: Joe Ascione interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: And then go play with Mark out at the 55 Bar in New York.

ctx.x: One avenue dries up but something else will hopefully replace it.

Yeah. And musically I like to plug in to different projects. I think that’s why when I tried a little Broadway thing I got bored very quickly. When I did some legit work, a little tympani or snare drum, and I have utmost respect for it and I love it, but I get bored quickly. And it’s probably my problem. But I don’t think it’s a problem. What I think it is is I like the spontaneity of the moment and the challenge of the project at hand. So whether it’s a gig or a two week engagement or a tour or a festival or a…
